mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the unemployment rate drops by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a surge in demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts increase by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face production challenges and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where industrial production decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal: a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to its 12-month moving average suggests strong consumer demand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative more frequently than positive when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal: during a period of economic expansion, a significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDP increases by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter during an economic expansion.
